source_notes: Recalled from open published data (Jane's-type references, service fact files) without web access; every uncertain figure is listed in estimated_fields. Epoch slotting follows docs/05 (E1 1950-59, E2 60-69, E3 70-79, E4 80-89, E5 90-2004, E6 2005-15, E7 2016-). Systems entering within ~1 year of a boundary are slotted at the epoch they actually defined, with the boundary noted in basis. Conventions: aircraft speed_kmh is max speed, road_range_km is combat radius (basis says which); ship speed_kmh is max speed converted from knots, road_range_km is cruise range, dims height is draft; helicopters use fuselage length. mass_t is loaded/full-load unless noted. gun_gen/radar_gen use the docs/11 G- and R-ladders. Nulls are deliberate: the US never fielded that role in that epoch, and the note says why -- absence is data. | 2026-08 normalization: measurement conventions per data/factions/CONVENTIONS.md (aircraft mass=MTOW; combat-aircraft range=combat radius with attested ferry kept in ferry_range_km; support-aircraft range=max unrefuelled range; helicopter len=fuselage with rotor_diameter_m separate and width=max airframe width; tank len=gun-forward; ship and submarine height=draught; submarine mass=submerged displacement; towed pieces carry null road range). Epoch boundaries follow the fielded-in-numbers policy (a system entering in the last ~year of an epoch sits where it was fielded in numbers); converted fields carry '| conv 2026-08' or '| audit 2026-08' notes in basis.
